record.original_question: Can one formulate a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity that unifies general relativity with quantum mechanics and remains mathematically coherent across the regimes where both are simultaneously relevant?

evidence.quote: Problem MPF3: Formulate a fully consistent theory of QG.

artifact.status_search_result: The unification of general relativity and quantum mechanics into a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity remains a major unsolved problem in theoretical and mathematical physics. While candidate frameworks such as string theory, loop quantum gravity, causal dynamical triangulations, and asymptotic safety have been developed, none has been established as a complete, mathematically rigorous and empirically validated theory of quantum gravity as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Quantum gravity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum gravity (QG) is a field of theoretical physics that seeks to describe gravity according to the principles of quantum mechanics... Despite many attempts, a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity has not been achieved.
status_evidence.claim: No complete consistent theory of quantum gravity is currently known.
